sources.entry: Tasmota - Open source firmware for ESP devices. Total local control with quick setup and updates. Control using MQTT, Web UI, HTTP or serial. Automate using timers, rules or scripts. Integration with home automation solutions. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C/C++

summary.one_liner: Tasmota is an open-source alternative firmware for ESP8266 and ESP32 family devices that provides web UI configuration, OTA updates, and fully local control over MQTT, HTTP, serial, or KNX.
summary.what_it_does: Replaces stock firmware on ESP8266/ESP8285 and ESP32-family microcontroller devices such as smart plugs, bulbs, and sensors. Configuration is done through a web UI, with OTA updates for later firmware versions. Control is available over MQTT (v3.1.1 or v5, to a local or TLS cloud broker such as AWS IoT Core or Azure IoT Hub), HTTP, serial, or KNX, and the device can run standalone without a server. Automation uses built-in Timers, Rules, and the Berry scripting language. The README also lists support for 150+ sensors and peripherals, lighting (dimmers, CT, RGB(W)(CW), addressable LEDs), Matter on ESP32, Zigbee/BLE gateway functions, and LVGL/HASPmota displays.
use_cases: flash smart plugs or bulbs with custom firmware
control ESP devices locally without a cloud service
connect ESP sensors to Home Assistant or openHAB over MQTT
automate devices with timers and rules
read temperature, CO2, or energy sensors on an ESP board
run Matter devices on an ESP32
how_to_run: Download a released binary or use the Tasmota WebInstaller for initial installation
Flash the firmware to the ESP device using the installation guide
Configure the device through its web UI or a device template
For custom builds, copy user_config_override_sample.h to user_config_override.h and compile with PlatformIO
notable: Runs on ESP8266/ESP8285 and the full ESP32 family, including Matter support on ESP32
Local-only control over MQTT, HTTP, serial, or KNX with no server required
Rules, Timers, and Berry scripting for on-device automation
Large sensor and peripheral set with a device template repository
Built-in WireGuard VPN client and ESP-NOW mesh (TasMesh) networking
caveats: Some features do not fit in precompiled binaries due to flash size and require compiling your own build
ESP8285 custom builds need DOUT flash mode and a 1M no-SPIFFS linker script; other flash modes may brick the device
Mains-connected devices carry electrocution risk; the README warns against flashing while plugged into AC power
Migrating between major versions may require stepwise upgrades, and minimal builds must be OTA-updated to a full build first
